title: Hornocker Cabin
description: The Hornocker Cabin was constructed in 1952 by Jess and Dorothy Taylor. It was later named after Maurice Hornocker who conducted research on Mountain Lions. The duplex is now used as an office space on one side, and a living space on the other.

title: Bridge Crossing Big Creek

title: Taylor Airstrip
description: Jess Taylor began constructing the Taylor Ranch airstrip in May of 1948. It took him approximately one year to complete the project due to the amount of brush and trees he had to remove. Jess used a team of 1,800 pound geldings and dynamite to remove the remaining stumps for the new landing strip.

title: DeVlieg Cabin
description: The biggest facility at TWRS was funded by the DeVlieg foundation after the loss of a bunkhouse and cookhouse that burned in 2000 (Diamond Complex Fire). Due to a large majority of the trees in the are burning, all of the materials to build the cabin had to be flown in.
rights: In Copyright - Educational Use Permitted. For more information, please contact University of Idaho Library Special Collections and Archives Department at libspec@uidaho.edu.

title: Lanham Cabin
description: The Lanham cabin originally was located on the Cabin Creek homestead. After finding out that the USFS was going to naturalize the site. Jim Akenson began planning how to transport the cabin to TWRS. His original plan was to float the logs down to Taylor. However, the U of I got in contact with the Idaho National Guard Engineering Division which ended up flying pieces of the cabin to TWRS as part of their summer training maneuvers in a Chinook chopper in June 1990.
rights: In Copyright - Educational Use Permitted. For more information, please contact University of Idaho Library Special Collections and Archives Department at libspec@uidaho.edu.

title: Hay Barn
description: Built in the August of 1985 by Jim Akenson and crew. A lot more went into the building of this hay barn than what meets the eye. Corner and wall posts were floated down Big Creek and then lifted out of the water by a pulley system. A mule team and stoneboat sled were used to move them to the building site. The site was on an old junkyard which had to be cleaned up along with removing the 400 pound boulders in the area. The rest of the building materials were flown in via three trips from Moscow.
